environment.description: Provider backend deployed on the same EKS cluster but fronted by an nginx ingress controller (v1.9.4) configured with annotation nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client: 'on' and nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-secret pointing to a namespace-scoped Secret containing a CA bundle (infra-team-ca). The ingress resource specifies nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-depth: '2' and nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-pass-certificate-to-upstream-header: 'ssl-client-cert'. The backend Service is ClusterIP (not externally reachable). A NetworkPolicy restricts ingress to the pod solely from the nginx ingress controller pods (label app.kubernetes.io/name: ingress-nginx). The CA bundle only contains certificates issued by the internal PKI operated by the platform-security team; client certs are issued per-service with CN=terraform-provider-<team> and have 24h expiry. The Terraform provider binary is compiled with a TLS transport that presents the client cert from a mounted Secret volume. No API key alone is sufficient to reach the backend—the TLS handshake must complete with a valid client certificate before nginx proxies the request.

config.network_policy: ingress only from pods with label app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx
